title: Only surviving child and his parents' advice about girls
summary: His siblings were stillborn; he tells how his parents told him to finish school before starting a family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Were you the only child in your family or did you have any brothers and sisters?

Well, I had two sisters, they were twins, and a brother, but they were all still births. I was the only one that lived, you know? And oh, I wish they were around now, you know? You know, after -- I think that's one of the reasons all the concentration came on me.
Oh, of course, that would make sense, sure.
You know? They weren't hard on me or anything like that, but they would always direct me. Oh, I'm going to tell a little funny story. I guess it's about time for that, maybe.
I was about third year high school, and
you know how a buy begins to walk the girls home carry their books for them and all that?

So for me to walk this little girl home, I would always have to pass by -- there was no way to get to her house but to pass by my house, and my mother would always sit in the front window. She knew exactly what time I was supposed to be there, which hour. And they sat me down, my father and mother sat me down at dinner, and they said one thing that has stuck. He says, "James, before you make us a family, finish school so you can support them." And you know, I've been reading ever since. That thing caught on to me, you know? I said I'd better be qualified here before I take on responsibilities, you know?
Yeah. Well, at least my head was spongey, then.
